title: Customer Security Obligation Mapping and Decision Scaffold for Enterprise Intake
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a decision scaffold that maps incoming enterprise security and compliance asks (SOC2/ISO controls, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA clauses, vendor questionnaires) to a standardized set of remediation paths, required evidence, SLA response tiers, and routing destinations. Goal: reduce manual Triage time, eliminate duplicate ask handling, and provide predictable commitments to sales and enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form fields updated to capture control-level asks and data residency constraints
Automated mapping rules cover at least 80% of common questionnaire clauses identified in prior analysis
Routing logic sends items to Compliance, Legal, or Solutions Engineering with recommended SLA tier and required evidence checklist
Decision scaffold documented in Confluence and approved by Security & Legal
Pilot with 3 enterprise accounts demonstrating 30% reduction in time-to-first-response and consistent SLA assignment
implementation_plan: Run clause clustering on recent 250 vendor questionnaires to produce a canonical clause taxonomy (Data Research)
Define mapping table between canonical clauses and internal controls / required evidence (PM + Security)
Prototype intake form UI changes in Console and non-Console submission schema for inbound emails/drive uploads
Build routing rules engine (lightweight rule set with override) in the intake service; add fallback to manual triage
Create SLA tier definitions and associate automated notification templates
Ship pilot toggle and monitor metrics for two weeks; collect feedback and iterate
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: Reviewed dataset of 250 questionnaires with Security. Key observation: 40% of clauses map to five control families (access, encryption, logging, retention, third-party). - Aisha

2026-03-05 - Decision: Use a hybrid approach — rule-matching for high-confidence clauses + human-in-the-loop for ambiguous ones. Engineering flagged risk of false positives impacting commitments. - Maya

2026-03-09 - Design review: DES team provided draft UI for intake form; agreed to add an 'I don't know' checkbox to surface ambiguous asks to Solutions Eng. Action: Design to provide accessible microcopy by 2026-03-12. - Lars (Design)

2026-03-11 - Engineering feasibility: ENG outlined two implementation options: lightweight rules engine in intake service (fast) or leverage existing policy service (longer but unified). Chose intake-service prototype for speed, with follow-up migration plan. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/intake/pull/418

2026-03-13 - Legal & Security sync: Approved mapping for SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 controls; asked for explicit retention language for GDPR/DPA routing. Security requested an audit log for every routing decision. - Priya Shah (Security)
2026-03-14 - PM note: Preparing pilot outreach list and SLA comms for Sales. Dashboard metrics to track: time-to-first-response, mapping-confidence-rate, routing-accuracy (manual override rate).
risks: Misclassification of clauses could lead to over-committing SLAs - mitigated by conservative SLA assignment and human review for low-confidence mappings
Dependency on ENG-4821 (routing infra) could delay pilot if not prioritized
Need for Legal sign-off on DPA wording could create gating for automated responses
Potential increase in manual triage if initial mapping confidence is low; track manual override rate closely
